title: SPEC B review and rewrite: cost, decomposition, stacked PRs

completion_criteria.text: SPEC B is reviewed line by line against the repository and its wrong or unreproducible citations are corrected, starting with the *_SCHEMA count and the figures no committed script reproduces.
The questions SPEC B leaves open are brainstormed to a decision, above all the instrument source in section 2.2 that section 8 names the single largest open question.
The two open research passes complete, and a cited report carrying the corrected architecture, the tree and sequence diagrams, and the gap analysis is produced and REVIEWED by the user.
The revised SPEC B is written and approved by the user, superseding the 2026-08-06 document, with every changed claim carrying a citation re-derived at the time of writing.
A successor thread is opened for SPEC B implementation, and this thread closes with no implementation work started.

spine.active_goal: Design and write a new SPEC superseding SPEC B: mitosis re-architected around an Agent SDK supervisor process, an orchestrator agent, human-in-the-loop, and context rotation.
spine.next_step: START HERE FRESH. 0328 fixes the order: research, REPORT, user review, then SPEC. (1) Run both open research passes - context usage versus accuracy scaled to WINDOW SIZE, so 250K and 1M get different thresholds; and the enforcement surface that makes instructions binding per 0326. (2) Re-ask the rotation trigger and orchestrator authority with those findings. (3) Produce the report via /report with tree and sequence diagrams. Do NOT write the SPEC until the user has reviewed the report.
spine.last_session: Six parallel agents established engine, harness and industry ground truth. Three blockers found; SPEC B Part III deleted by 0325. User corrected the variance requirement. Decisions 0325-0328 recorded and c5 inserted. Research, diagrams, report and SPEC all deferred at 104% context.

open_risks.text: A Workflow cannot ask a human mid-run and resumes same-session only — human-in-the-loop is impossible inside the Workflow runtime, which is one of the three reasons orchestration moved to an SDK supervisor
Nothing inside Claude Code reads a spawned subagent's context fill — the rotation trigger has no sensor unless the supervisor hosts the orchestrator itself and reads ResultMessage.usage

Agents guess instead of escalating in 55.8-67.8% of runs, with explicit refusals at or below 2.5% — trusting the SPEC requires an engineered uncertainty-detection step, never a prompt instruction telling the implementer to raise concerns

Naive compaction drops constraints 30-59% of the time while verbatim pinning restores 0% at under 0.5% of context — decisions, constraints and failures must be append-only and never pass through a summarizer on rotation

The 20-25% context premise is a practitioner heuristic, not a finding — RULER measured effective context at 16-100% of claimed window and degradation tracks absolute tokens, so any threshold must be re-derived per window size

Rotation mid-flight has no story yet — orphaned child agents, in-flight dispatches and duplicated side effects such as a double PR need an in_flight registry plus idempotency keys on (run_id, step_id)

Re-derive every figure the rewrite keeps, or mark it carried-and-unverified — a SPEC arguing that nothing may be tuned before it is measured cannot itself rest on numbers no committed script reproduces
Keep implementation out of this thread entirely — its criteria are research, report and writing only, and a successor thread owns every code change the SPEC calls for

Do not switch branches in the primary checkout if the cutover is ever rolled back — live config entries resolve into the release today, but a rollback repoints them at the working tree and restores the hot-swap hazard
Give every sub-agent dispatch run_in_background false — parent agents end their turns believing they are blocking on background children, and the dispatched work is silently lost

Several harness facts came back UNDOCUMENTED and may need zero-agent probes before the SPEC commits to them — the budget global's shape, the journal.jsonl structure, the transcript directory layout, and the agent-resumption contract

key_decisions.title: SPEC B is reviewed and rewritten in its own thread before any implementation thread opens
Orchestration leaves the Workflow sandbox for an Agent SDK supervisor process
Zero variance means instructions are binding, not that model output is reproducible
A new SPEC supersedes SPEC B rather than amending it in place
The architecture report is produced and reviewed before the superseding SPEC is written
The rotation trigger is an absolute token count, calibrated before it is fixed
The orchestrator judges inside phases and never reorders, skips or re-runs them

out_of_scope: Implementing any part of SPEC B, which a successor thread owns
Editing SPEC A or the config staging and promotion machinery it shipped
The fix pipeline, excluded by the user from both SPECs
